title: Slow-timescale regulation of dopamine release governs recovery of a motivational drive over days
title_zh: 缓慢时间尺度的多巴胺释放调控支撑动机驱动在数日内的恢复
abstract: The rise and fall of a motivational state can unfold over many days. We used mouse mating behavior to model how the brain orchestrates such slow-timescale changes in motivation. Male mice become sexually satiated after successful matings, and their motivation to mate recovers over a week. Using deep-brain fluorescence-lifetime imaging in the medial preoptic area (MPOA), we found that tonic dopamine transmission-which regulates mating drive-also declined after mating and gradually re-emerged across several days. Two mechanisms regulated dopamine transmission. First, successful mating transiently reduced the tonic firing of hypothalamic dopamine-releasing neurons, thereby inhibiting dopamine release and mating behavior for 1 to 2 days. Second, these neurons' ability to produce and release dopamine dropped after mating and recovered over the following week, paralleling the recovery of mating drive. Therefore, changes in neuronal firing rate and neurotransmitter composition cooperate to control the early and late phases of motivational dynamics, respectively.
abstract_zh: 动机状态的兴起与消退可能在多天时间尺度上发生。我们以小鼠交配行为模拟大脑如何协调此类缓慢的动机变化。成功交配后，雄性小鼠会出现性饱足，其交配动机需一周才能恢复。通过在内侧前视区（MPOA）进行深层大脑荧光寿命成像，我们发现，调节交配驱动的强张性多巴胺传递在交配后下降，并在数天内逐渐恢复。两种机制调控多巴胺传递：第一，成功交配短暂降低了下丘脑多巴胺能释放神经元的强张性放电，从而抑制多巴胺释放和交配行为1至2天；第二，这些神经元合成和释放多巴胺的能力在交配后下降，并在随后的一周内恢复，与交配驱动的恢复同步。因此，神经元放电率与神经递质组成的变化分别协作控制动机动力学的早期和晚期阶段。
